result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the fear of difference—the instinctive distrust, hatred, or dehumanization of those who are unlike us in race, religion, gender, nationality, or any other arbitrary divide.

This single change would cascade into the dissolution of wars, oppression, and systemic injustices rooted in "us vs. them" thinking. Empathy would replace prejudice, cooperation would outpace competition for resources, and the energy wasted on conflict could be redirected toward solving shared problems like poverty, climate change, or disease.

It wouldn’t make humanity perfect, but it would strip away the most corrosive force in our history: the belief that some lives matter less than others. The rest—justice, peace, progress—would have room to grow.

(And yes, I’m aware this is an impossibly idealistic answer. But if we’re dreaming, I’d rather dream big.)
